instruction: I'm studying with music playing in VLC media player. Sometimes I accidentally scroll my mouse wheel over the volume control and the volume goes extremely loud, disturbing my concentration. Could you help me set a maximum volume limit to 100% so the volume can't exceed normal levels?

parameters.window_name: lecture.pdf — 6.006 Introduction to Algorithms, Lecture 2: Data Structures

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires user to set VLC's maximum volume to 100%. The evaluator uses existing check_qt_max_volume metric to verify that qt-max-volume setting is set to 100 in VLC config file.
metadata.verification: Verified using existing check_qt_max_volume function. Expected value: qt-max-volume=100. Default is 125.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly checks the exact VLC setting (qt-max-volume) that controls maximum volume limit
Getter logic (get_vlc_config) correctly extracts VLC configuration file from OS-specific paths
Metric logic (check_qt_max_volume) correctly parses config file and validates the qt-max-volume setting against expected value
Expected value (100) is semantically correct for limiting volume to 100% as specified in instruction
Postconfig appropriately restarts VLC to ensure configuration is persisted to disk
Complete instruction coverage - the single requirement (set max volume to 100%) is fully verified
Edge cases properly handled: missing config file, missing setting (defaults to 125), type conversion
Data flow is correct: getter extracts config → metric parses and compares → returns pass/fail
